1993 IEE Colloquium on Connectors on Vehicles (Digest No.1993/228)
abstract: There has been much said already about automotive wiring and connectors and this paper seeks to concentrate more specifically on the electrical connector which has been developed for the heavy goods vehicle, bus and off highway industries including agriculture. This connector is a two-part assembly containing one or more electrical contacts which when connected has an engagement seal and integral wire seals which will resist the ingress of the most penetrating of substances, not least that associated with high pressure steam cleaners.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical contact and connectors in automotive systems
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Connectors on Vehicles (Digest No.1993/228)
abstract: Presents a review of electrical contact phenomena applied to connectors, and associated with the special conditions of automotive systems. Electrical contacts are often the weakest link in an electrical system in terms of long term reliability. The reliability of the contact interface is affected by a complex interaction of environmental effects, materials and circuit factors. The systems used in automotive systems are particularly susceptible to the environmental factors, such as temperature fluctuations, vibration and corrosion. With the increasing complexity of automotive electronics the careful design of connectors and other contacts must be considered as an important matter. This paper considers recent trends in connector design, and presents a novel method of assessing connector reliability using a nonlinear contact resistance probe.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Connectors on Vehicles (Digest No.1993/228)
abstract: It has long been the established view that the much maligned connector is the biggest cause of automotive electrical system failures. This may well have been the case five years ago, though the findings of the Automobile Association aided with an improved system of reporting failures at the roadside and a more comprehensive analysis of breakdown statistics, are that the position has improved substantially. In terms of the size of the problem for the AA, roadside failures due to faulty connectors are well down the scale. This statistic seen against the growth of the number of connectors in the modern automobile, makes the improvement in connector quality, specification, and application even greater than the present statistics reveal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Connectors on Vehicles (Digest No.1993/228)
abstract: Following worldwide recession, the automotive industry is likely to see sustained growth from 1993 onwards, as recovery continues. Historical connector concerns are considered, and ways of overcoming the most abundant faults are outlined. Emerging and predicted technologies within the automotive connector industry are discussed. The aim is to analyse new techniques rather than developments of the traditional connector technologies, in particular with regard to environmental protection and connector application. The future of the automotive connector industry is predicted in terms of market forces and product trends.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rationalisation as a route to reliability
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Connectors on Vehicles (Digest No.1993/228)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to offer an insight into some alternative thoughts for increasing the reliability of vehicle connector systems, without resorting to complicated testing procedures or long, drawn-out development programmes with connector suppliers. Put in simple terms, the paper will attempt to explain the benefits of using a greatly rationalised number of connector types on a vehicle to try to achieve the ultimate goal of a perfect electrical wiring system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

abstract: The requirements can be approached using developments in the following areas:- (i) Design the connector and harness to be suitable for cut, strip, terminate and block machines. The author discusses the features necessary for the connectors for the above emphasising the advantages of a modular form of connector housing and tables one family of connectors which demonstrates this philosophy. (ii) New contact materials. The author discusses the need for these new materials and illustrate the advantages of some of those available.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Failure mechanisms in stationary low current contacts
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Connectors on Vehicles (Digest No.1993/228)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to highlight the ways in which stationary low current contacts can fail. It begins by describing the various categories of components that the term 'contact' embraces and gives a few simple definitions in order to qualify the analysis. The main section focuses in on individual failure mechanisms and describes them in more detail. In order to provide a coherent analysis the various mechanisms have been groups into broad bands. At the highest level these are 'chemical' and 'mechanical' and refer to the prime effect of a particular mechanism. These have then been divided and sub-divided until at the lowest level the individual mechanisms are given. In this way a tree type structure is formed, giving a hierarchy of failure mechanisms. This also helps to illustrate their interdependence. It is hoped that this paper will act as a review to new readers to the subject. While no area has been analysed in great detail, a suitable reference list has been included for those readers who wish to examine specific topics in more depth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
